Defining where to show toolbars
===============================

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page Aug 24, 2026 · [126 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars/_history)

**Toolbar display rules** tell the plugin which files to display toolbars on, in this order:

1.  based on a property;
2.  based on a rule (such as the folder the file is in); or
3.  by default, if no other rules apply.

Note

For positioning of a toolbar within a note, read about [Positioning toolbars](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Positioning-toolbars)
.

Property
--------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#property)

Set the `notetoolbar` property on any note with the name of the toolbar you want to display. Set that note's property to `none` to not display a toolbar at all for that note.

Change the name of the property to use by by changing the `Property` setting. This property always overrides any other rules, such as for folders.

Tip

While a note is open, right-click on a toolbar (long-press on mobile) and select **Swap toolbar...**\* to swap the current toolbar with another you can choose.

If you don't use properties, or prefer not to use them, read on to learn about Rules (available in `v1.35+`) or Folder Mappings (`1.34 and earlier`).

Default toolbar
---------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#default-toolbar)

A **Default toolbar** is displayed on all notes, unless a property or other rule is satisfied (i.e., they take precedence over the default toolbar).

*   You will be asked after creating your first toolbar if you wish to set it as the Default.
*   Using a folder mapping or `folder path` rule of `*` will do the same thing.
*   To show toolbars in other file types, see: [Show toolbars in other files](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#Show-toolbars-in-other-files)
    .

Tip

In `v1.35` or later: To create an even more specific set of conditions as to when a default toolbar appears, create a rule at the bottom of your list with `folder path is *`.

Rules
-----

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#rules)

> Available in `v1.35` and later

Open the Rules window from settings, or with a command: `Note Toolbar: Open rules`:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/master/docs/images/rules.png)

### Conditions

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#conditions)

A rule consists of one or more conditions for each toolbar, including checking parts of file, folder, or tag names:

| Compare... | using... | with these options / notes... |
| --- | --- | --- |
| editor mode | is • is not | ...`editing` or `reading` |
| file name | contains • does not contain • starts with • ends with • is • is not |     |
| file type | is • is not | ...any of the [file types](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-types)<br> supported by Note Toolbar, including manually entered types (e.g., `excalidraw`) |
| folder path | contains • does not contain • starts with • ends with • is • is not | Use a _folder path_ of `/` for files in the root folder, and `*` for _all_ files. |
| platform | is • is not | ...`desktop`, `mobile`, `phone`, or `tablet` |
| tags | contains • does not contain • is empty • is not empty |     |
| _any property_ | exists • does not exist • is empty • is not empty • contains • does not contain | For checkbox properties, use _contains_ `true` or `false` |

### About precedence

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#about-precedence)

The order in which rules are listed here matters:

*   Files are matched to rules starting from the top of the list.
*   If you have a property on a given note, it will override the rule.

Drag a rule up or down to change where it is in the list.

### Notes

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#notes)

*   The Rules format replaces _Folder Mappings_ (folder mappings will be converted into Rules on plugin update).
*   Create a rule for _No toolbar_ if you don't want to show a toolbar under a provided set of conditions.
*   If you open the Rules window while you have a file open, the actively applied rule is highlighted.
*   If any [File types](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-types)
     you want to display toolbars for are not enabled, the Rules window will show an error.

Folder mappings
---------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#folder-mappings)

> Available in `v1.34` and earlier. Replaced with Rules in `v1.35` or later.

Open the **Note Toolbar → Display rules** section to use folders your vault files live in to determine what toolbar should appear:

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/master/docs/images/settings_rules.png "Rules section of the settings, defining where to show the toolbar")

For example, if your daily notes are all in the same parent folder, just specify that folder and map it to your "Daily Notes" toolbar, and it will appear on all existing, and new daily notes.

### Special folder mappings

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#special-folder-mappings)

| Folder | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Maps toolbars for notes that _just_ live in the root folder. |
| `*` | Applies toolbars for _all_ of your notes (note that you can still override this with more specific folder mappings or the property). |

Tip

Map a toolbar to `*` at the bottom of your Folder Mappings, to create a "fall-back" toolbar that shows when no other toolbars are set for your note.

### About precedence

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#about-precedence-1)

The order in which mappings are listed here matters:

*   Notes are matched to folders starting from the top of the list.
*   If you have a property on a given note, it will override the folder mapping.

Drag a mapping up or down to change where it is in the list.

Related settings
----------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#related-settings)

### Show toolbars in other files

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#show-toolbars-in-other-files)

Open the **Note Toolbar → [File types](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-types)
** settings section to add enable toolbars in audio, bases, canvases, images, PDF, videos, and more.

Notes:

*   Any references to properties in variables or script expressions won't work, as these file types don't have properties.
*   In all of these file types, toolbars in the `Below Properties` position are shown at the Top position instead.

### Toolbars within the app

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#toolbars-within-the-app)

Open the **Note Toolbar → [Toolbars within the app](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Toolbars-within-the-app)
** settings section to enable toolbars in other areas of Obsidian such as the File menu, the New tab view, the Ribbon (on phones), and when text is selected.

### Swap toolbars

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Defining-where-to-show-toolbars#swap-toolbars)

While a note is open, right-click on a toolbar (long-press on mobile) to show an option to swap the toolbar with another you can then choose. Selecting an option will update the Note Toolbar property in the current note (`notetoolbar` by default).

![](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/17337703/418352281-7f76705c-1b07-454c-be55-aafe29c4dba6.gif?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..DUq7YpjO9XllPLN_Wa6WxtfzrArTTIQducNWnp15qjo)

Notes:

*   Select the "Default" option to remove the property, which reverts to the default (folder) mapping.
*   Note that Swap toolbars will not be available if:
    *   the active file is not a note/markdown (as there's no properties to change); or
    *   your Note Toolbar Property is set to `tags` (to prevent accidental deletion/overwriting of note tags).

* * *

Note Toolbar URIs
=================

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page Apr 10, 2026 · [33 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs/_history)

**Note Toolbar URIs** are links that you can use to execute commands, focus on folders, open menus (only within [Note Toolbar Callouts](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-Callouts)
), and open toolbar settings... all from within your note's contents.

Make sure URIs are wrapped in angle brackets `<` `>` (when used within Obsidian) or properly [encoded](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#encoding)
.

Example of using Note Toolbar URIs within [Note Toolbar Callouts](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-Callouts)
:

```md
> [!note-toolbar]
> - [Command URI](<obsidian://note-toolbar?command=workspace:toggle-pin>)
> - [Folder URI](obsidian://note-toolbar?folder=Demos)
> - <hr>
> - [Menu URI](obsidian://note-toolbar?menu=Tools)
> - [Menu URI with ID](obsidian://note-toolbar?menu=7fb30215-d92c-43ce-8158-b79096672bd1)
```

Tip

All URIs support a `vault` parameter, which you can use to specify the vault to open, before executing a command. For example, `obsidian://note-toolbar?vault=Personal&command=...` opens the Personal vault before executing the command.

Options available:

Execute Commands
----------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#execute-commands)

**Format**

```ini
obsidian://note-toolbar?command=COMMANDID
```

Notes:

*   Use the [Copy URI for command](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Commands#Copy-URI-for-command)
     command to get the URI, or [use Advanced URI](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/How-to-get-a-URI-with-Advanced-URI)
    .
*   You can use either `command=` or `commandid=` as both work the same.

Link to Folders
---------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#link-to-folders)

Focuses on the given folder in the file explorer. This has the same behavior as clicking on a bookmarked folder.

**Format**

```ini
obsidian://note-toolbar?folder=FOLDERNAME
```

Open Menus
----------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#open-menus)

Opens the given toolbar as a menu. This works only when used within [Note Toolbar Callouts](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-Callouts)
.

**Format**

```ini
obsidian://note-toolbar?menu=TOOLBAR_NAME or TOOLBAR_ID
```

Open Toolbar Settings
---------------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#open-toolbar-settings)

Opens the settings for the current, or provided toolbar.

**Format**

Open the current toolbar on the current note's settings:

```ini
obsidian://note-toolbar?toolbarsettings
```

Open the settings of the provided toolbar (if it exists):

```ini
obsidian://note-toolbar?toolbarsettings=TOOLBAR_NAME
```

Notes when using URIs
---------------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#notes-when-using-uris)

Items to be aware of when using URIs:

*   URIs don't appear to work in notes that were opened in a new window, as the focus is returned to the main window on click. If that's not suitable for you, use [data elements](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-Callouts#via-data-elements)
    .

### Encoding

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs#encoding)

Make sure to [escape URIs](https://help.obsidian.md/Editing+and+formatting/Basic+formatting+syntax#Escape+blank+spaces+in+links)
 (when used within Obsidian) in angle brackets `<` `>` if the URI contains special characters like `:`. Otherwise, you must properly encode your URIs, which means converting special characters into a code. You can do using an online tool like [this one ↗](https://www.urlencoder.io/)
.

Example encodings:

*   becomes `%20`
*   `:` becomes `%3A`
*   `/` becomes `%2F`
*   `%` becomes `%25`

Example URIs with escaped special characters:

```md
> [!note-toolbar]
> - [Toggle pin](<obsidian://note-toolbar?command=workspace:toggle-pin>)
> - [Toggle pin](obsidian://note-toolbar?command=workspace%3Atoggle-pin)
> - [Tools Menu](<obsidian://note-toolbar?menu=Tools Menu>)
> - [Tools Menu](obsidian://note-toolbar?menu=Tools%20Menu)
```

What makes Note Toolbar different from other plugins?
=====================================================

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/What-makes-Note-Toolbar-different-from-other-plugins%3F#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page Jul 19, 2024 · [5 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/What-makes-Note-Toolbar-different-from-other-plugins%3F/_history)

How is Note Toolbar different from [Commander](https://github.com/phibr0/obsidian-commander)
?
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/What-makes-Note-Toolbar-different-from-other-plugins%3F#how-is-note-toolbar-different-from-commander)

Commander’s a great plugin, but there’s definitely some big differences:

*   Note Toolbars can be scoped to notes. (Commander is more about adding options to existing UI, not tied to notes.)
    *   Note Toolbar allows you to create different toolbars with options for different use cases (e.g., create a toolbar specific to your Daily Notes, with navigation for next/previous day, etc.).
*   Note Toolbars appear at the bottom of Properties, right within your notes. With Note Toolbar Callouts you can also add them in the middle of your notes. (Both are not within Commander’s options.)
*   Note Toolbar allows you to link to URIs, files, _and_ commands. You can also sub in your note’s properties and title into URIs as variables. (Commander only allows you to execute commands.)

File items
==========

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-items#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page Jul 6, 2026 · [15 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-items/_history)

**File** items allow you to open a specific file, or highlight a specific folder, from your toolbar.

After selecting the **File** item type, search for any file within your vault, including other file types (e.g., PDFs, images). You can also link to folders, which when selected in the toolbar, will reveal the folder in the file explorer (just like bookmarking the folder).

To link to files _outside_ of your vault, use [URI items](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/URI-items)
.

Tip

When clicking on a file item in the toolbar, you can use [modifier keys](https://help.obsidian.md/User+interface/Tabs#Open+a+link)
 to open it in a new tab, tab group, or window.

Advanced settings
-----------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-items#advanced-settings)

Clicking on the gear (⚙️) icon opens advanced options:

### Where to open file

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/File-items#where-to-open-file)

Choose where to open files: _Default_ (current tab), in a _Modal_ (read only), _New tab_, _Split pane_, or in a _New window_.

*   By default, files will open in the current tab.
*   Using modifier keys when clicking on file items will override this setting.
*   Modal window width can be adjusted (on desktop) via [Style Settings](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Style-Settings-plugin-support/)
    .
*   When opening files in modals, set the **Use originating file as context** option to specify that the active file that opened the modal should be used as context on rendering.
    *   For example, this allows you to open a Base file that shows backlinks in a modal, and have it show the backlinks in the file that _opened_ the modal.
    *   To specify a different file altogether to use as context, see the `ntb.modal` [Note Toolbar API](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-API)
        .

Creating toolbars from callouts
===============================

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-toolbars-from-callouts#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page May 29, 2025 · [16 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-toolbars-from-callouts/_history)

Create toolbars from [Note Toolbar Callouts](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-Callouts)
 that you may have created, or may have been shared with you, in one of two ways:

*   Import a callout into a new or existing toolbar in settings; or
*   Right-click on a callout and select _Create Note Toolbar from callout_

Import callout items into an existing toolbar
---------------------------------------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-toolbars-from-callouts#import-callout-items-into-an-existing-toolbar)

Use the import button (above the toolbar's item list).

![](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/17337703/375497255-0b82104e-f5f4-40f9-9880-3e9425c5f908.gif?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..vzyVlGSwSLD_Cy1WnzrponaGRsdMsAosXLVfz7vg2Ik)

Notes:

*   The callout's heading is not required. If provided, styles, and the imported callout toolbar name, are ignored.

Right-click on a callout
------------------------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-toolbars-from-callouts#right-click-on-a-callout)

Select some Note Toolbar Callout markdown in a note, then right-click and select _Create Note Toolbar from callout_. This will attempt to import the callout as a new toolbar.

The callout must start with `> [!note-toolbar]` in order to be recognized.

What's supported
================

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-toolbars-from-callouts#whats-supported)

How callouts are translated back into toolbars:

*   The toolbar's **name** is used if provided at the end of the first line of the callout, unless you are importing a callout into an existing toolbar.
*   Toolbar **styles** (except custom styles) are imported if they're valid, unless you are importing a callout into an existing toolbar.
*   **Icons** are imported if they're built-in to Obsidian (Lucide) and in [Iconize](https://github.com/FlorianWoelki/obsidian-iconize)
     format (e.g., `:LiHome:`).
*   **Tooltips** are imported from comments at the end of each line.
*   **Data elements** and **[Note Toolbar URIs](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-URIs)
    ** can be imported for command/menu/folder items, and are translated into the appropriate item types.

See [creating callouts from toolbars](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Creating-callouts-from-toolbars)
 to see how toolbars can be exported to callouts. All of the supported features noted there can be imported again.

* * *

INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md
========================================

[Jump to bottom](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#wiki-pages-box)

Chris Gurney edited this page Apr 2, 2026 · [5 revisions](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md/_history)

[obsidian-note-toolbar](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/index.md)
 / [INoteToolbarApi](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.md)
 / NtbMenuItem

Defines a menu item that can be dynamically created and displayed via [`ntb.menu()`](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/Note-Toolbar-API#menu)
.

Properties
----------

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#properties)

### icon?

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#icon)

> `optional` **icon?**: `string`

Optional icon to display in the menu item.

* * *

### id?

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#id)

> `optional` **id?**: `string`

Optional ID to add to the menu item when it's rendered.

#### Since

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#since)

1.27

* * *

### label

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#label)

> **label**: `string`

Label for the menu item.

* * *

### type

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#type)

> **type**: `"command"` | `"file"` | `"uri"`

Type of the menu item. Can be `command`, `file`, or `uri`.

* * *

### value

[](https://github.com/chrisgurney/obsidian-note-toolbar/wiki/INoteToolbarApi.Interface.NtbMenuItem.md#value)

> **value**: `string`

Value for the menu item. For `command`, this is the command ID.
